bcc.description: Addresses that get a hidden copy, at most 10. Each one is checked against the suppression list, and one suppressed address stops the send. Not with `template.id`.

capture_engagement.description: Whether the email's engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) are captured as analytics events of the recipient. They count as analytics events. Defaults to on for `template_key` and `template.key` sends, and to the project's setting for `template.id` sends.

cc.description: Addresses that get a visible copy, at most 10. Each one is checked against the suppression list, and one suppressed address stops the send. Not with `template.id`.

from.description: Sender, as `security@example.com` or `Example <security@example.com>`, on a verified domain of the project. Without it, rendered content goes out from the project's default sender, and a template from its own sender. Not with `template.id`.

headers.description: Extra email headers by name, such as `X-Entity-Ref-ID` or `List-Unsubscribe`, at most 10. Values are printable ASCII up to 870 characters. Headers PostHog sets itself, such as `From`, `Subject` and `Content-Type`, are refused. Not with `template.id`.

html.description: HTML body of the rendered email. Only with `template_key`.

identifiers.description: Who the email is for, used to attribute engagement events.

distinct_id.description: Distinct ID of the recipient's person. The email's engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) and the send itself are recorded against that person. Defaults to the recipient's email address. The template can't read the person's properties, so pass everything it needs in `message_data`.

message_data.description: Data for the template's Liquid placeholders, available as `variables`. For example `{"reset_link": "https://..."}` fills `{{ variables.reset_link }}`.

reply_to.description: Addresses replies go to. Not with `template.id`.

subject.description: Subject of the rendered email. Only with `template_key`.

tags.description: Name and value pairs, at most 10, that PostHog adds to the email's engagement events as `$email_tags`. Not with `template.id`.

name.description: Tag name: ASCII letters, numbers, `_` and `-`. Names starting with `ph_` are PostHog's.

value.description: Tag value: ASCII letters, numbers, `_` and `-`.

template.description: The template to send, by key or by id. Leave it out to send content your code rendered, with `template_key`.

hash.description: Content hash of the template you hold, as `v1:` and 64 hex characters. When PostHog never published that content, the send answers `template_outdated` and sends nothing. Only with `key`.

id.description: ID of the template, for templates made in PostHog. Give either `key` or `id`.

key.description: Key of the template, as uploaded with `PUT /api/projects/@current/messaging_templates/by_key/{key}/`. Give either `key` or `id`.

template_key.description: Names an email whose content your code rendered, such as `password-reset`, so its metrics, logs and status group under it. Send it with `subject` and `html` or `text`, instead of `template`. PostHog sends the content as is and never stores it as a template.

text.description: Plain text body of the rendered email. Only with `template_key`. Without it, PostHog derives the text from `html`.

to.description: Email address of the recipient, as `jane@example.com`.
